name: Chateau La Cheneviere
positioning: A former 18th-century manor house in a 12-hectare park in Normandy, 10 kilometers from Bayeux
best_for: Travelers exploring the D-Day landing beaches
Garden lovers who want a historic country estate

facts.text: The hotel is a former 18th-century manor house set in a romantic park.
The manor house was completely restored in 1988.
The hotel sits in a 12-hectare park that includes 2 hectares of walled gardens.
A lime-lined avenue leads to an English garden surrounding the manor house.
The grounds have Cedars of Lebanon, ginkgo biloba trees and centuries-old sequoias alongside a collection of old roses.
Each room has its own decoration, combining old charm with modern comfort.
The rooms feature wood paneling and marble fireplaces.
The heated outdoor pool has a small children's pool at its end.
Guests staying at the chateau have open access to a tennis court.
The kitchen garden is cultivated using permaculture principles and supplies herbs, fruits and vegetables to both restaurants.
Le Botaniste, the fine-dining restaurant in the chateau, serves cuisine inspired by nature and its garden.
Bayeux is 10 kilometers from the hotel.

highlights.text: La Cheneviere has its own authorized helipad, a starting point for helicopter tours over the WWII landing beaches, Arromanches, Deauville and Honfleur.
During World War II the chateau was occupied by the Germans, and then by the Americans after the D-Day landings.
The hotel can organize guided e-bike tours of the D-Day landing beaches.
The heated outdoor pool is reached by crossing the park along tree-lined paths into the walled garden.

considerations.text: The outdoor pool is open only from mid-May to mid-September, and guests are advised to contact reception for the exact dates before booking.
The hotel sits about 1 kilometer before the roundabout at Port-en-Bessin; it can arrange transfers from Bayeux station, Caen, Deauville and the Paris airports.
WhataHotel notes the countryside location means you need transportation to explore the area.
